chunks: From him, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The price of the dog that does not hunt is unlawful gain (suh't).
He said, 'And there is no objection to the price of the cat.'

key_terms.سُحْتٌ: Unlawful gain or consumption of wealth without right

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling a dog that is not used for hunting in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In the context of *tahdhib al-akham*, this narration clarifies the economic principle of *suh't* (unjust enrichment) by linking the utility of an animal to the legitimacy of its sale price. While non-hunting dogs are deemed to have an unlawful price due to their specific commercial use in hunting, cats are permitted because their primary value lies in pest control rather than specialized trade, reflecting the Shia juristic focus on intent and utility in commercial transactions.
